reply.title: Why does a sigmoid squash any number into 0 to 1?
reply.story:
When modeling probabilities or neural activations, we often need to take any real number—ranging from negative infinity to positive infinity—and map it smoothly into a restricted range between zero and one. A linear function fails because it grows without bound. We need a curved transition that flattens out at both ends.

The logistic function achieves this by placing the input inside an exponential denominator. As the input grows very large and positive, the exponential term shrinks toward zero, driving the overall fraction to one. As the input drops toward negative infinity, the exponential term grows massively, driving the fraction down to zero.

By adjusting the steepness and the midpoint, we can control how abruptly this transition occurs. The derivative at the center reveals the maximum sensitivity of the curve, showing how a smooth S-shaped path naturally bounds any input.
reply.cardDescription: Explore how the logistic sigmoid maps any real number into the interval from $0$ to $1$. Adjust the steepness and midpoint to see the S-shaped transition curve.
reply.instructions: Adjust the steepness and midpoint sliders to observe how the logistic curve stretches and shifts.
